interface.title: Field Logger v2.0 (gps-field-logger)
interface.field: GNSS/GPS field surveying and agronomic field trials (experimental design for field measurements)
interface.stage_of_work: data collection in the field: designing the session, then logging it as it happens
interface.what_it_is_for: A single-page, offline-capable logbook. You define scenarios and blocks, it generates a randomized complete block design (RCBD) visit schedule, and it times each point, records receiver power-on/RTK-fix times and weather, and exports the session as CSV or JSON.

data.note: There is no demo data. I typed everything in: session '2026-10-30_North Farm'; receivers Swift Duro and Emlid Reach RS2; scenarios 'Under canopy' (🌳, with a description) and 'Open sky'; blocks 'North Field' (notes 'Corn, flat') and 'South Field'; coordinates 42.03, -93.62. Weather for those coordinates came back as 46.4°F, Partly Cloudy, 83% humidity, 2.6 mph wind. Data persists in localStorage: the finished session was still listed after a page reload (screens/037.webp).

features.name: Weather capture with fallback location methods
features.general: Attach the current weather to a record. Try automatic location first, then a place-name search, then typed coordinates. Errors show a retry; the reload control on the result card clears it and returns to the method choice.
features.specific: Weather panel: Use My Current Location (GPS) → Or search by place name → Enter coordinates manually (Lat/Lon/Go). The card shows °F, condition, humidity, wind, coordinates and fetch time. ↻ clears the card and shows the method chooser again.
steps: press Use My Current Location
on error press Try Again to get the method chooser back
search a place name, or open 'Enter coordinates manually'
type Lat/Lon and press Go
read the weather card; ↻ clears it and returns to the method chooser, so the location must be given again

features.name: Instrument start-up timer cards (power-on → fix → TTFF)
features.general: For each instrument in a list, stamp when it was switched on and when it reached a usable state. The card shows the elapsed time, and the instrument can no longer be deleted once switched on.
features.specific: GPS Receivers list: add by name; each card has ⏻ Power On (stamps time, hides ✕) and 🎯 RTK Fixed (enabled after power-on), and shows 'TTFF → RTK: Ns'. At least one RTK fix is needed before BEGIN DATA COLLECTION appears (per source).
steps: type receiver name and press + or Enter
press ⏻ Power On
press 🎯 RTK Fixed when the receiver reports a fix
read the TTFF badge; repeat for each receiver
serves_tasks: Log each instrument's start-up and time to first good fix

features.name: Factor-level list editors with a time-budget estimate
features.general: Enter the treatments and the blocks as editable lists with optional descriptions, and set per-point timing; a running estimate of total points and total time follows the settings.
features.specific: Measurement Scenarios (name, description, icon picker, 🗑) and Study Blocks (name, notes, 🗑). Collection Settings (Static Duration, Travel+Setup, GPS Height) feed 'Est. total time: P pts × N min = H hrs', updated when a field loses focus.
steps: add scenarios (choose the icon before typing the name)
add blocks with optional notes
set static duration / travel+setup / GPS height
leave the field and read the updated time estimate
serves_tasks: Define the treatments or conditions to be measured
Define the blocks (spatial or treatment groups)
Set timing parameters and see the time budget

features.name: Seeded RCBD schedule preview with re-shuffle
features.general: From the treatment and block lists, randomize treatment order within every block from a shown seed, list the resulting visit order with point IDs, and re-draw it before committing; the seed is kept with the record.
features.specific: 🎲 RCBD Schedule Preview: 'Seed: N | B blocks × S scenarios = P points', grouped by block, point IDs like B2_Open_sky, ↻ Re-shuffle draws a new seed; BEGIN DATA COLLECTION locks the shown order.
steps: add at least one scenario and one block to see the preview
press ↻ Re-shuffle until the order suits, noting the seed
press BEGIN DATA COLLECTION to lock the schedule
serves_tasks: Generate and check a randomized complete block design

features.name: Guided point-by-point collection with timeline and re-collect
features.general: Walk through a randomized list one item at a time with a start/stop timer and a progress bar. A timeline grouped by block shows what is done. Any completed item can be reopened, flagged with a reason from a fixed list, and measured again; the redo count and latest reason are kept.
features.specific: Collect tab: Point #N card (scenario, block, visit, point ID) with ▶ START COLLECTION / ■ END COLLECTION, live seconds timer and 'n / 4 points completed'. The timeline is grouped by block. Tapping a completed point opens a review card with 🔄 RE-COLLECT THIS POINT. The reason sheet offers Equipment issue / Tripod bumped / Wrong location / Obstructed / Correction link dropped / Weather interference / Other. The point resets to PENDING with 'Re-collect #1' and a ×1 badge.
steps: press START COLLECTION
press END COLLECTION (advances to the next point)
tap a completed point in the timeline to review it
press RE-COLLECT THIS POINT and choose a reason
collect the point again
when all are done, use JSON / CSV / Finish
serves_tasks: Time each scheduled measurement in randomized order
Flag a bad measurement with a reason and redo it

features.name: Two-format session export (sectioned CSV + full JSON)
features.general: Export the whole record in two formats: a table file with the measurement rows followed by instrument, treatment, block and session-metadata sections, and a structured file holding the complete session object.
features.specific: 📊 CSV and 📋 JSON on the '✅ All N points completed!' panel and on the past-session view; files named gps_<session_name>.csv/.json. The CSV omits weather lat/lon and scenario icons; the JSON has them, plus status and seed.
steps: finish all points to reach the completion panel
press 📊 CSV
press 📋 JSON
later, re-export the same files from the past-session view
serves_tasks: Export the session record in tabular and structured formats
Review a past session and export it again

features.name: Session archive with read-only summary
features.general: Keep finished sessions on the device. Open any one to see a summary of conditions, design, instruments, the timed schedule and notes; discard an unwanted in-progress session.
features.specific: PAST SESSIONS list (start screen and History tab). The session view shows date, weather, '2 blocks × 2 scenarios = 4 pts | 1min | 1.5m', scenarios, blocks, receivers with TTFF, 'LOCATIONS — SEED: 559462' timeline and notes, with JSON / CSV buttons; the summary timeline does not show the ×1 re-collect badge. History also has 🗑 Discard Current Session.
steps: press Finish on a completed session
click the session under PAST SESSIONS
review the summary
← Back
to drop an unwanted session: History tab → 🗑 Discard Current Session → confirm
serves_tasks: Close the session and archive it
Review a past session and export it again

screens_never_reached: Successful device-GPS weather fetch: the headless browser has no geolocation permission ('Location permission denied', screens/003.webp)
Place-name search results: the geocoding request for 'Ames Iowa' returned 'No location found' (screens/005.webp), probably because the geocoding API was out of reach
Help / GitHub pages: external links (github.com), not allowed
not_done: Weather by device GPS and by place-name search were dead ends here: Use My Current Location gave 'Location permission denied' (screens/003.webp), Try Again returned to the chooser (screens/004.webp), and searching 'Ames Iowa' gave 'No location found' (screens/005.webp). Only manual coordinates worked.

Redoing a point erases its original times: per the source (recollectLocation, gps-field-logger.html:496) start_time and end_time are set to null, so only Recollect_Count and the latest Recollect_Reason survive. This contradicts USAGE_GUIDE.md's 'the original timestamps are preserved'. The past-session summary also does not show the ×1 re-collect badge (replay, t13).

Exports disagree with the screen in two places: Swift Duro TTFF is 2s on screen (screens/010.webp, screens/029.webp) but TTFF_s=3 in the CSV (the JSON stores rtk_fixed_at with .000 ms while powered_on_at keeps ms). Point 1 shows 1s on screen but Duration_s=2 in the CSV.
The CSV has no weather lat/lon and no scenario icon; the JSON has both. The JSON exported before Finish has status 'collecting' and a leftover _preview_schedule.
Static Duration is not enforced: points can be ended after 0–2 s with a 1-minute setting (screens/027.webp shows a 0s duration).
Editing a Collection Settings number re-draws the form and erased text already typed in Field Notes. Picking a scenario icon erased the typed scenario name. Both had to be retyped.

Clicking the 💾 header button had no visible effect in the run (screens/033.webp). Per the source it is forceSave, which writes the active session to localStorage and briefly flashes the button (gps-field-logger.html:516).
Clicking the icon of a saved scenario had no visible effect (screens/034.webp); its purpose is unknown.
I did not try deleting a receiver with ✕ or deleting a block with 🗑, and did not use the Travel+Setup or GPS Height fields beyond seeing them carried into the export.
